card.title: 1st SAN MARCO
card.text: Deployment: Gets +2+2 and Blitz if there is a Navy card on top of your deck.
card.flavorText: The 1st San Marco Regiment is the Italian Navy’s elite marine infantry unit, with roots dating back to 1713. At the start of WWII the regiment was composed of two battalions, but it was later expanded to seven. Its first engagement was during the invasion of Yugoslavia in April 1941, where the regiment carried out successful landings on several islands in the Adriatic and seized ports against minimal resistance. The 3rd Battalion of the San Marco Regiment gained fame and its nickname "Tobruk" during the British commando raid on the night of 13-14 September 1942, repelling the attack and capturing 200 enemies. In spring 1943, the San Marco Regiment fought hard in Tunisia to defend the Mareth Line, especially during the Battle of Wadi Akarit, where the Tobruk Battalion was destroyed.  German General Hans-Jürgen von Arnim, the last commander of Axis forces in North Africa, later commented that the San Marco Marines were "the best soldiers I ever commanded".  Following Italy’s surrender in September 1943, most San Marco troops joined the Allies, while the 4th Battalion continued fighting for the Axis until 1945. Known for their discipline and combat effectiveness, the San Marco Regiment proved itself as one of Italy’s most formidable units in WWII.
